requirements-and-traceability.title: Requirements and Traceability
requirements-and-traceability.description: Requirements, their refinement structure, and typed links to delivery artifacts.
requirements-and-traceability.extension_scope: Requirement identity, requirement-to-requirement relations, and traceability from requirements to external artifacts.
relation_rules: Requirement relations preserve the source and target roles declared by the owning aggregate.
Traceability terms run from a requirement to an artifact and remain distinct from inverse graph-projection terms.
non_ambiguity_constraints: A requirement is not an implementation artifact, test result, evidence artifact, or document.
Lexically equal terms with opposite endpoint roles do not share a canonical term.

architecture-and-boundaries.title: Architecture and Boundaries
architecture-and-boundaries.description: Operational assets, documents, structural containment, communication, trust, and access boundaries.
architecture-and-boundaries.extension_scope: Architecture participants and structural relations that describe deployment or operational context.
relation_rules: Structural relations describe the directed role of one architecture participant relative to another.
Boundary relations do not redefine risk, control, evidence, or traceability semantics.
non_ambiguity_constraints: An operational asset is not an observation or evidence record about that asset.
Containment, access, communication, dependency, and data flow remain distinct relation meanings.

threats-risks-and-controls.title: Threats, Risks, and Controls
threats-risks-and-controls.description: Risk scenarios, threat models, controls, findings, audits, verification, and risk-control mappings.
threats-risks-and-controls.extension_scope: Risk analysis, control implementation and testing, findings, audit scope, and verification outcomes.
relation_rules: Risk and control relations preserve whether the source mitigates, is mitigated by, assesses, protects, or maps another participant.
Structural mapping edges remain distinct from direct domain relationships.
non_ambiguity_constraints: A mapping node or scoped implementation is not interchangeable with the control or risk participant it references.
Verification-result-to-requirement VERIFIES is distinct from requirement-to-artifact traceability VERIFIES.

evidence-and-observation.title: Evidence and Observation
evidence-and-observation.description: Evidence artifacts, observations, source provenance, supersession, and evidence-bearing relations.
evidence-and-observation.extension_scope: Recorded observations and durable evidence that support governance and assurance conclusions.
relation_rules: Evidence relations point from the governed subject to the evidence that supports it unless a term explicitly declares the inverse.
Supersession preserves direction and must not be collapsed with its inverse.
non_ambiguity_constraints: The subject of evidence is not itself evidence.
OBSERVED_ON and OBSERVED_IN retain their distinct endpoint roles.

workflow-and-process.title: Workflow and Process
workflow-and-process.description: Execution, lifecycle, and process concepts that coordinate engineering work.
workflow-and-process.extension_scope: Workflow participants, lifecycle records, and process relations not owned by a narrower domain family.
relation_rules: Process concepts may organize domain artifacts without redefining the artifacts' native meaning.
Lifecycle relations preserve the declared before, after, and dependency roles.
Workflow reporting runs and phase-event relations remain read models and never become execution authority.
non_ambiguity_constraints: Workflow state is not evidence, requirement status, or research provenance.
Process association does not imply implementation, verification, or control effectiveness.
A workflow work-item reference identifies an external issue tuple and is not a first-class work-item aggregate.

contracts-and-invariants.title: Contracts and Invariants
contracts-and-invariants.description: Published contracts, invariant declarations, and governed conformance concepts.
contracts-and-invariants.extension_scope: Machine-readable contracts and invariants that govern externally consumed or workflow-critical surfaces.
relation_rules: Contract concepts constrain another family without taking ownership of that family's domain vocabulary.
Conformance relations identify the contract and the subject being constrained.
non_ambiguity_constraints: A contract declaration is not the runtime implementation it constrains.
An invariant is not treated as enforced unless a named structural gate proves it.

research-and-provenance.title: Research and Provenance
research-and-provenance.description: Research runs, research artifacts, provenance nodes, and upstream-to-downstream provenance relations.
research-and-provenance.extension_scope: Research workflow records and the evidence lineage connecting sources, intermediate artifacts, claims, and prose.
relation_rules: Provenance edges run from upstream input to downstream output as declared by ADR-069.
Research artifacts and provenance records remain distinct from the content they identify.
non_ambiguity_constraints: Research provenance SUPPORTS is not the same relation as one operational asset supporting another.
CITATION, derivation, selection, and contribution remain separate provenance meanings.
